**Verdict: NOT CLEAN** — one significant visual bug in the 3D scene.

## (1) Overlapping / clipped UI
- **DOM layer is fine.** Header, title, timestamp, and both buttons are well-spaced with no collisions. The canvas bleeding past the bottom edge is expected for a scrollable report.
- **In-scene overlap (the real problem):** A huge light-blue grid plane rises from behind the grass and fills the entire upper-left sky area, visibly intersecting the green ground plane. It reads as a mis-scaled and/or mis-rotated mesh (ground/water plane rotated wrong, or a grid helper with a runaway size), not intentional scenery.

## (2) 5-second comprehension
- Partially. The title ("Project Report") and Print/Close buttons are instantly clear, so the *page type* is understood.
- But the *content* fails the test: there are zero design elements visible (no patio, plants, fence, furniture — just an empty grass grid). A new user would assume the design is missing or the render failed. The blue plane actively reinforces the "something is broken" impression.

## (3) Confusing / ambiguous / broken-looking
- **Blue sky-plane (high severity):** dominates the frame and looks like a rendering error. Likely fix: correct the plane's rotation (it appears tilted ~30–45° instead of horizontal) or clamp its scale so it sits below the horizon.
- **Stray wireframe lines** extend off the grass into the blue background with no clear purpose — adds to the "unfinished" look.
- **Empty report:** if the project genuinely has no objects, the scene should say so (e.g., "No items placed yet") rather than showing a bare plane.
- Minor polish: both header buttons are the same solid green — "× Close" would read better as a secondary/ghost style; the scene also lacks any scale bar, compass, or axis hint.

**Fix priority:** repair or remove the oversized blue grid plane and add at least the designed elements (or an empty-state message) — those two changes would resolve most of the confusion.

# QA Review: Backyard Designer 3D

## (1) Overlapping or clipped UI

No hard overlaps found, but the bottom edge is **very tight** in three places — worth verifying at shorter viewports:

- **"Patio" list item vs. status bar** — the last sidebar item sits flush against the "Tool: Raise…" bar. It renders fully here, but any shorter viewport will clip it with no breathing room.
- **"Sun & Shadow" button / scale bar / "Sun" toggle vs. status bar** — same crowding; they nearly touch the status strip.
- **Right-edge chart button** (bottom of the zoom/reset stack) — also ends just above the status bar.

Everything else is clean: the Terrain Sculpting panel clears the bottom toolbar row, Take Tour clears the compass, and the top toolbar items all fit with room to spare.

## (2) 5-second comprehension

**Mostly yes.** Logo, "Getting Started" tip, an item catalog with pictures, and a big 3D yard communicate the concept instantly. The weak spot is the **bottom command cluster**: two rows of buttons (Terrain/Sun & Shadow + Tape Measure/Terrain/Excavate/Analyze/Innovate) plus the floating panel is a lot of competing controls for a first-time viewer.

## (3) Confusing / ambiguous / broken-looking

- **"FPS: 2"** in the status bar — the most broken-looking thing on screen. Either the app is genuinely crawling (performance problem) or the counter is wrong. Either way it undermines confidence.
- **"Terrain" appears three times** — panel title, green panel-toggle button (bottom-left), and brown active tool button (bottom-center) — with *two different active states*. Users can't tell what each one does or why both look "on."
- **"Innovate"** — vague label; no icon hint about what it does (AI suggestions? presets?).
- **"Strength: 0.05"** — raw float with no unit or scale; compare to Brush Size's friendly "8 ft."
- **"Daytime" pill** floating at the top-center of the canvas has no visible affordance — is it a dropdown, a label, a button?
- **Tiny unlabeled icon** at the right of the "Terrain Controls" header — purpose unclear.
- **Blue wireframe** surrounding the green terrain may read as "unfinished/broken" to newcomers, though it's presumably the sculptable grid (likely intended).

**Verdict: not CLEAN** — layout is fundamentally sound with no true overlaps, but the FPS: 2 reading, the triple "Terrain" labeling, and the cramped bottom edge need attention before ship.
